Aside from page views, unique visitors, orders and revenue, what do you look at on a daily basis to see what direction you are going?

I'll start.

  1. RPV (revenue per visitor = revenue/unique visitors) * this is my absolute #1 metric for several reason
  2. Conversion Rate (orders/unique visitors)
  3. AOV (revenue/orders)
  4. Items per Order (Lines/Orders)
  5. Bounce Rate (percentage of visits with only a single page view)
  6. Pages per Session (page views / visits)
  7. Shopping Cart Abandonment Rate ((Cart Opens - Orders) / Cart Opens)

In my experience I can't tell you what a 'good' RPV would be for example. It's all going to depend on what your fixed costs are so what I tell people is to look at these for trends. Whether your site is doing well or poorly, it's critical you understand why.
What are your go to KPI's(calculated metrics) for measuring success?

Good list. As a marketeer, the big one two which aren't on your list: Cost and ROAS. I also keep a very close eye on New vs Returning to validate that our retention and re-engagement strategies are working as we would expect.
Using Measurement Protocol, I import Cost of Goods Sold into Google Analytics so we can calculate and see actual profit from web sales. A lot of up front effort, but totally worth it.
This is the holy grail of web analytics and a great call out.

I went through a bunch of tutorials trying to get my start, but these were the ones that helped me the most. I'm a big fan of Bob Tabor's teaching style, and these helped me a lot:

C# for Absolute Beginners - very useful language that leverages the .NET framework to make your life easier.

Windows Phone 8.1 Development for Absolute Beginners - I like this one because not only am I WP fan, this will teach you XAML, which is a very intuitive way to design the same sort of clean, minimal UIs that W8 (on phone, tablet, and Desktop) applications use.

HTML5 and CSS3 for Absolute Beginners - self explanatory, necessary building blocks for any web developer.

JavaScript Fundamentals for Absolute Beginners - again, self explanatory.

All of this is free, your progress is tracked. High quality videos, all come with downloadable source code (from Channel 9) for comparison if you can't get yours working.
Microsoft Virtual Academy - some great "Absolute Beginner" courses I want to share.
